title: Mind, consciousness and AI seminar
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
purpose: Study current research on the metaphysics of mind: scientific and philosophical theories of consciousness (higher-order, representationalist, global workspace and integrated information theories), the hard problem and illusionism, panpsychism and the combination problem, mental causation, the self, and whether artificial intelligence systems, including large language models, could understand, be conscious or have moral status.

weeks.2: Physicalism, the explanatory gap and the hard problem
weeks.4: Global workspace and integrated information theories
weeks.6: Panpsychism, Russellian monism and the combination problem
weeks.8: The self, personal identity and the brain
weeks.9: AI and understanding: from the Chinese room to language models
weeks.10: Could an AI system be conscious? Theories, indicators and tests
weeks.12: Writing and presenting a seminar paper

blocks.deliverable: Write a response paper on the explanatory gap.
Compare how two theories explain the same experiment.
Week 7 midterm; write a seminar paper proposal.
Evaluate an argument about whether language models understand.
Submit a seminar paper draft for review.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Seminar paper: write a 5,000- to 7,000-word seminar paper on one question (the hard problem, illusionism, the combination problem or AI consciousness) that surveys the literature accurately, reconstructs the strongest opposing view and offers an original argument; revise it after written feedback.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
